name: RNS
group: NaviCath Ltd. (R. Beyar co-founder) with Rambam Medical Center / Technion; clinical sites also Fundeni Hospital and Shaare Zedek (beyar2006_remote p. 296-297)
versions: 2005 concept, design and pre-clinical studies (EuroIntervention 2005;1:340-5, cited as weisz2013_safety ref. 1; not read); 2006 JACC first-in-human pilot (beyar2006_remote); described as the basis of CorPath 200 (crinnion2022_robotics; no full text states that NaviCath became Corindus)
devices_driven: standard 0.014-in coronary guidewire and the angioplasty device (balloon or stent); the guiding catheter is hooked to the RNS but not driven; the two devices are interlocked: 'When the guidewire is manipulated, the device is locked at its position and vice versa' (beyar2006_remote p. 296-297). Rapid-exchange devices per wagener2024_features (not stated in beyar2006)
n_dof_detail: 3: wire axial and rotation (optionally discrete 30-degree steps), device axial (beyar2006_remote p. 296)
translation_detail: friction-roller (device: motored roller pair with a passive motion-sensing roller pair behind it, beyar2006_remote p. 296, Fig. 2B; wire: 'mechanical transmission module', type N.R.)
rotation_detail: wire navigator rotates the wire through a mechanical transmission module (type N.R.) (beyar2006_remote p. 296)
force_sensing: no force sensor named: motion-sensing rollers report slippage of the motored rollers and the system halts; 'any force that exceeds a threshold causes system stall' (beyar2006_remote p. 296, 299)
haptics_leader: no: computerised touch-screen control console and joystick (beyar2006_remote p. 296, Fig. 3); haptic force feedback named as future work (p. 299)
imaging_compat: standard fluoroscopy screens; the protocol kept the operators at the bedside (beyar2006_remote p. 299)
sterility: detachable wire and device navigators on a sterile plastic-sheet-covered base; Y-connector in a sterile holder (beyar2006_remote p. 296, Fig. 2 caption); disposable status N.R.
validation_detail: glass coronary model; anaesthetised sheep (number N.R.), 14 coronary branches, 8 stents implanted; first-in-human pilot: 18 patients (15 men, 3 women) at 3 centres, single-vessel PCI (beyar2006_remote p. 297); 20 lesions per wagener2024_features Table 1 (lesion count not stated in beyar2006)
key_numbers: wire crossed the lesion in 17 of 18; stent delivered in 15 of 17; technical success 94% (guidewire) and 83% (overall procedure); clinical success 100%; fluoroscopy time 8.8 +- 4.8 vs 9.1 +- 3.5 min with standard technique (NS); catheterisation time 44 +- 32.7 vs 61 +- 19 min; diameter stenosis 60.6 +- 13.5% -> 17.0 +- 7.8%; no in-hospital MACE (beyar2006_remote p. 296-298)
